plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with cup-shaped flowers atop sturdy stems and broad, blue-green leaves. Thousands of cultivars exist, ranging from single and double forms to fringed and parrot types. Late-season tulips peak in cool temperate gardens in late April.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late spring (April to May in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Netherlands, northern Europe, North America, and temperate gardens worldwide; wild ancestors from Central Asia
plants.funFact: In the 1630s, tulip bulbs in the Netherlands became so valuable that single bulbs sold for more than the price of a house during 'Tulip Mania'.

plants.name: Wisteria sinensis
plants.description: A vigorous woody climbing vine that produces long, pendulous clusters of fragrant pea-like flowers before or as the leaves emerge. It can climb tall trees, pergolas, and walls, and live for decades.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late spring (April to May)
plants.location: Native to China; widely cultivated in Japan, Europe, and the United States
plants.funFact: Wisteria vines twine counterclockwise, while the Japanese wisteria (Wisteria floribunda) twines clockwise, which helps tell the species apart.

plants.name: Cardamine pratensis
plants.description: A delicate perennial of damp meadows and stream banks with pinnate basal leaves and loose clusters of four-petaled flowers. It appears around the time the cuckoo returns to Europe and is a key food plant for the orange-tip butterfly.
plants.location: Damp meadows, wet grasslands, and woodland edges across Europe, northern Asia, and parts of North America
plants.funFact: It is the main larval host plant for the orange-tip butterfly, whose caterpillars feed on its seed pods.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tall tree with fern-like foliage that is famed for its spectacular displays of trumpet-shaped blue-purple flowers. In the Southern Hemisphere, flowering usually happens in spring, but in some regions of South America and Africa, scattered late blooms appear in autumn.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere (October to November), with a secondary autumn bloom around April in some warm regions such as parts of Australia and southern Africa
plants.location: Native to South America (Argentina, Bolivia); widely planted in South Africa, Australia, and subtropical cities worldwide
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, thousands of jacaranda trees line the streets, earning it the nickname 'Jacaranda City'.
